biography: Humberto Guerra Jr. wasn't born into racing royalty, but his passion for speed was ignited early, watching Ayrton Senna replays with his grandfather in São Paulo. His father, a mechanic, nurtured this love, building Humberto his first go-kart from spare parts. Humberto spent his teenage years tearing up local karting circuits, earning a reputation for his relentless consistency. His big break came at 21 when he won a regional championship, earning him a spot in a junior formula series. After a rocky start to his car racing career, Humberto found his footing in endurance racing, proving his ability to maintain blistering pace while managing tire wear with uncanny precision. This led to his current seat with MetalMoro MRX Honda P3, where he aims to prove himself as one of the top talents in Brazilian motorsport.
drivingStyle: Humberto is known for his smooth, calculated driving style. He isn't the flashiest driver, but he's incredibly consistent and rarely makes mistakes. He focuses on maximizing corner exit speed and maintaining momentum, often sacrificing entry speed to achieve this. Tire management is one of his greatest strengths; he can nurse a set of tires longer than most, allowing him to run longer stints and gain track position. While calm under pressure, Humberto can become fiercely competitive when challenged directly, often resulting in wheel-to-wheel battles that showcase his defensive prowess.

rivalries.reason: A fierce on-track battle for the championship in their junior formula days led to a lingering competitive tension.
Ricardo is perceived as a 'pay driver' who earned his seat through money, and Humberto openly criticizes this system. They frequently clash on and off the track.
Both have very similar driving styles and are closely matched in terms of pace, often leading to strategic battles on the track with each trying to outsmart the other.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of socks his grandfather gave him for good luck.
Listens to a specific playlist of Brazilian samba music before every race.
Meticulously cleans his helmet visor before each session, regardless of how clean it already is.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about pushing to the absolute limit every second; it's about finding the rhythm and dancing with the car."
careerHighlight: Winning the 6 Hours of Interlagos in 2022, securing a last-lap overtake to take the lead and the victory for his team.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the Brazilian GT Championship in 2021 due to a mechanical failure, costing him the championship.
